walkthroughs.title: Breathlessness when lying down and swollen ankles

doorway: I cannot catch my breath when I lie down, and my ankles have become swollen.
Vital signs are available on the chart.
Perform a focused history and physical examination, discuss your plan, and document only what you obtain.

plan.notice: Breathlessness when lying down and swelling suggest a fluid problem but do not by themselves identify its cause.
plan.pivot: Ask how many pillows are needed, whether breathlessness wakes the patient and how swelling or weight has changed. Clarify medications and adherence without blame.
plan.exam: Assess respiratory comfort, JVP, lungs, heart and peripheral edema; keep each observation distinct from the diagnosis of heart failure.
plan.avoid: Confusing orthopnea with paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea or using edema alone to prove heart failure.

goals: Link orthopnea, PND, edema and weight change.
Medication access is clinically relevant history.
Use heart, lungs and neck together to assess congestion.

recall.prompt: Before naming a diagnosis, what is the key distinction in this presentation?
recall.answer: Ask how many pillows are needed, whether breathlessness wakes the patient and how swelling or weight has changed. Clarify medications and adherence without blame.
